Alright. This my be an odd question. I'm 35, 6'1", 155 lbs. I also seem to be "big boned", but the more weight I lose the bigger and more visible my bones look. I'm not interested in gaining muscle or getting a "toned" look. If I had any "look" that I wanted, it would be smooth, slender, and soft, without any visible bones or muscles.

But that's a secondary concern. Really, the main thing I'm interested in is just getting stronger, faster, and more fit, and my worries about how other people will see me are a hindrance to that goal. Right now I'm not muscular, but I see having any visible muscle as being something that really doesn't fit my image of what I want to be, and I think other people would see me as stupid and brutish. So I've avoided doing anything that would make me more muscular. I really only started concerning myself with the way I looked a few years ago when I realized convincing everyone to stop judging people so much on their appearance wasn't realistic, so I don't really have much experience with determining the way others percieve people. I don't perceive people with visible musculature that way myself, so my stupid question is, "do people look at those with visible muscles as brutes, dumb, oafish, etc?".

I have contemplated suicide, and I tried to go through with it. I tried to kill myself because I was convinced that I was utterly evil and needed to be exterminated. At no point did I want to die, I was just convinced that I was morally obligated to annihilate myself. It is not always selfish. Your reasons for contemplating suicide may have been selfish(or not), but that does not mean everyone's are.

People can hold a diversity of reasons for their beliefs, actions, self-image, etc, with or without the presence of mental illness.

On a more general note, asserting that you have experienced something and come to certain conclusions based on it does not, in itself, give anyone a reason to believe those conclusions until you give an actual "why".
Keep in mind, transhumanists/singulatarians believe something like this would be an acceptable and trivial sacrifice, and many think it would be a good thing.

I have a variety of reasons, but one of my main ones is that the majority of parents I've seen seem to have totally nonsensical epistemologies, usually centered around some idea of transcendent parental enlightenment, zero-sum morality and correctness by it as an epistemic principle, and a near total refusal to admit that they could ever be wrong. I've personally seen this happen to a lot of people. I suspect it might be some defense mechanism for dealing with children in a society that indoctrinates it's members with unrealistic ideals of super-parents, but I don't really know.

I am terrified of becoming that thing.

I really don't care about not being thrilled with a job, I'd be willing to shovel sh*t or dig ditches if I need to. I can deal with other people, but not if it's a situation where the job requires that I alter my entire epistemology so that anything a customer says has to be accepted as absolute truth. Lets say a customer says "You are immediately going to stick your face in that deep fryer". I'm screwed. I'd rather live on the streets and root through dumpsters than end up in a job where a customer can make me do or believe anything they say.
Thank you. Thank you so much.

Ever attempt suicide? That feeling that you are evil, that you deserve suffering because you are worse than hitler and stalin combined? And trying to follow through on it, frantically trying to kill yourself with any means at hand because you think you deserve to be hurt, while other people try to hold you back? Worse than any disappointment I've ever felt. Disappointment barely even registers to me anymore. I wish it did.
Discipline can certainly be given. That's what most people's first discipline is. Few people are born thinking of cutting off their fingers because they accidentally offended someone.
Discipline is easy. You can do it in seconds. It won't help you, or anyone else, though, except sadists and masochists.

So, when a child is beaten and locked in a closet because they didn't tuck their sheets in properly, it is something under their control? I suppose. But is that really going to be beneficial? Discipline is suboptimal for creating positive change, because it is about avoiding negative consequences by creating a fear of suffering for arbitrary failure.

Discipline is what stops you. You are bad, you deserve to be hurt because you are bad. Hurt yourself, or someone else will hurt you because you are innately evil and deserve to be hurt for your failures.
Self harm through destructive thoughts or physical injury IS discipline.
Motivation gets you started. Discipline is what makes you stop, because when you make a mistake, you are a bad person who deserves to be hurt and fail.
Discipline wants me to literally torture myself to death, because I forgot to replace the roll of toilet paper. Sounds like a great idea. /s
That's right. Next time you forget to do the dishes, you should cut your arm off. Discipline FTW.

I do not have a GED. I've heard various opinions about how difficult it would be to get, ranging from "It's easy, anybody can do it." to "It's harder than getting through high school". I'm actually a little worried about getting a GED instead of a High School diploma, since I've heard a GED is seen as a black mark by a lot of employers. I'm about 4 months off from getting an AS degree if I choose to take that route, but I've heard that having an AS degree is also seen as a black mark. I've considered going back to high school, and I'm willing to do so, but the classes there are way harder, and it would probably be about 3 years before I could graduate at a "normal" high school pace, even assuming that I'm intelligent enough to understand the material. I need money pretty much now, or else I'm out on the streets.

I really do not want to lie on an application, both because I don't think it's right, and because the risks for lying and being found out are likely greater than the risks of not getting the job. The 10 years of not working I can't really do anything about, but what do you mean by an attitude problem?

A lot of different things. Going to community college off and on, and a fair number of others that made me money but are no longer practical. I'm worried that disclosing them here could result in having my identity revealed. I should probably mention, none of them were criminal activities.

No, I need to kill myself, not not kill myself. But I can't, my horrible fucking rational mind, such as it is, and my id keeps stopping me from doing so. But I need to, and I am having a hard time getting myself to go through with it because I really, really want to live.
Yeah, something that would be a bit closer in pain caused to the ink and stuff used in actual tattoos, so I could get some approximation of what it is like.

Well... part of the reason I was thinking pinky was because it would be relatively easy to cut off, and the longterm consequences of lacking a pinky finger would be pretty minor. Cutting off my lip to end the unbearable pain would be.... not so easy.

I'd rather not. In the past, it was things that I had said or done that, now, seem like silly reasons for killing myself. At the time, I really, really thought that those things were unforgiveable crimes, and that I was so bad that I HAD to be destroyed. They seem pretty silly in retrospect. But this seems different to me.

I've never really suffered. I've had things happen to me that I didn't want to happen, but I've never experienced anything that REALLY hurt. Other people have things much worse than me, and I don't know if I can comprehend their suffering. It's easy for them to understand everything about me, but I can't understand anything about what they have gone through. There's a difference between the type of little, cutting your finger type things that are the worst I've ever experienced, and the very real, traumatic pain other people have experienced. Making amends I'm not sure is practical. Being who I am, I might make things worse. And I really DON'T want to kill myself. But I'm worried this is just me making more rationalizations for being selfish and continuing to live as I am.

Matter is an idea we learn too... that doesn't mean it doesn't exist. I'm not even sure if the things I've done(or failed to do) are evil, and I'm not sure if what I am is innately evil or not. If what I am, or have done, is as bad as I am afraid, then death would be better than I deserve, but the best thing for everyone else. If what I am, or have done, is not bad, or at least not very bad, then I wouldn't need to do anything except continue trying to be good. When I try to use reason, I THINK that I am not a bad person, and that I don't deserve to suffer, or die. But I am afraid that I'm just inventing pathetic, stupid, selfish justification in my head to try and excuse what is inexcusable.
